action: Relay operators: upgrade to Tor 0.4.9.17 as soon as possible and watch for further releases.
date_note: Date of the 0.4.9.17 release; the flood is described as ongoing with no stated start.
exec: Tor-dependent services and users may see slow or unreliable connections while the attack continues.
geo_basis: country of the Tor Project; the attack source and affected relays are worldwide
plain: The Tor anonymity network is being flooded with traffic that overloads its volunteer servers, and its developers issued an emergency software update to cope.
summary: The Tor Project released Tor 0.4.9.17 on November 13 after a flood of client circuits overwhelmed relays, which it says affected most relay operators. The release counts IPv6 clients by /64 prefix in its denial-of-service defences and removes the directory authority bastet's keys over a possible compromise. Tor has not named the attacker and expects further releases.
title: Tor Project ships emergency relay update 0.4.9.17 as client-circuit flood overloads relays

validation.note: CyberInsider and eSecurity Planet read and agree; both relay the Tor Project announcement, which was not reachable (forum page 404, changelog 403). Golem could not be read past its consent wall.

review.note: CyberInsider and eSecurity Planet: Nov 13 release, circuit flood, most relay operators, /64 IPv6, bastet keys removed, attacker unnamed; Tor primary not reachable.
